In this article, I’ll walk through the seven chairs in [Steelcase’s lineup](https://www.btod.com/refurbished/) and give you my honest opinion on each one: from the entry-level Series 1 all the way up to the Gesture.

* * *

### TL;DR: The 20-Second Verdict

I ranked the six most popular Steelcase office chairs to help you understand which model fits your needs, budget, and body type.

- **The Good:** Steelcase’s lineup covers different price points and use cases. The Leap offers best overall adjustability, Series 1 delivers budget-friendly ergonomics, Gesture excels for multi-device users, Think balances simplicity and support, Karman provides premium mesh, and Amia offers comfortable upholstered seating.
- **The Bad:** All Steelcase chairs command premium prices. The most popular models (Leap and Gesture) start above $1,000, and choosing between similar models requires understanding subtle differences in adjustment philosophy and design.

**Bottom Line:** The Leap remains the best all-around Steelcase chair for most users. The Series 1 is the value pick in the Steelcase lineup.

* * *

Full Disclaimer: We are an office furniture dealer and sell some of the Steelcase office chairs we review. To learn more about the products we sell, our review process and why you can trust us, please visit: [Why we’re different. Who is BTOD.com and The Learning Center?](https://www.btod.com/blog/who-is-the-breakroom-blog-why-you-can-trust-us/)

* * *

### Jump To A Section

- ➔ [2\. Series 2](https://www.btod.com/blog/6-most-popular-steelcase-office-chairs/#series2)
- ➔ [3\. Amia](https://www.btod.com/blog/6-most-popular-steelcase-office-chairs/#amia)
- ➔ [4\. Karman](https://www.btod.com/blog/6-most-popular-steelcase-office-chairs/#karman)

- ➔ [7\. Gesture](https://www.btod.com/blog/6-most-popular-steelcase-office-chairs/#gesture)

[![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/office-chair-guide-blog-768x120px-1.jpg)](https://www.btod.com/chairlist/)

* * *

### 1\. Series 1 Office Chair

**2026 Price: $507.00 \| [Buy on Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3OPYGfC)**

The Series 1 is the entry point into the Steelcase lineup, starting around $490. It comes with four-way adjustable arms and a solid variety of upholstery options. The frame build quality is genuinely impressive for the price — the molds and stitching on the seat and backrest make it one of the better-looking chairs in the $500 range.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/steelcase-series-1-why-pick.jpg)

The seat pad has a nice amount of give and provides adequate support. The four-way adjustable arms do feel a bit cheaper and harder compared to Steelcase’s pricier options, which is the main trade-off at this price point. Still, for a [highly rated ergonomic chair](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-reviews/) under $500, it’s hard to beat.

* * *

### 2\. Series 2 Office Chair

**2026 Price: $714.00 \| [Buy on Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3zS6dWS)**

The Series 2 bridges the gap between the Series 1 and higher-tier chairs like the Amia or Think. Starting around $588 with the airbag option and four-way adjustable arms, it can climb closer to $900 with the headrest and upholstered backrest.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/steelcase-series-2-why-pick.jpg)

This chair features the same four-way adjustable armrests first introduced on the Leap V2, which is a meaningful upgrade over the Series 1 arms. The lumbar support paired with the Air Live Back technology offers solid lower support without being overly aggressive — a good balance for most users.

* * *

### 3\. Amia Office Chair

**2026 Price: $999.00 \| [Buy on Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3Jq9joh) or [Refurbished on BTOD.com](https://www.btod.com/steelcase-amia)**

I would highly recommend the Amia for most people. Priced just around $1,000, it offers almost everything you need in a high-end ergonomic chair for long hours of sitting. It features the same four-way adjustable armrests found on the Leap V2, and the backrest includes Live Back technology with height-adjustable lumbar support for full back coverage.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/steelcase-amia-why-pick.jpg)

The seat pad on the Amia is my personal favorite in the entire lineup — it provides outstanding sitting support for eight-plus hour days. The tilt function is basic with an upright tilt lock only, which is the main trade-off versus the Leap. Best suited for small to large body types, but not recommended for users over 6’3″ or above 250–275 lbs.

* * *

### 4\. Karman Office Chair

**2026 Price: $1,099.00 \| [Buy on Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3KbttnN)**

The Karman is the newest addition to Steelcase’s lineup, available for around $1,100 in a variety of color options with four-way adjustable armrests. My overall experience has been positive — I enjoy the flexibility and movement it offers. Unlike the weight-activated mechanism on the Series 1 and 2, the Karman has a full recline feature with 20° boost activation.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/steelcase-karman-why-pick.jpg)

The mesh seat with integrated padded cushioning is comfortable for long hours without pressure points. My only wish is that the lower lumbar support were a bit more aggressive. The armrests have a similar adjustment range to the Leap V2, but the pads feel more rubbery and firm. For more detail, see our [full Steelcase Karman review](https://www.btod.com/blog/karman-steelcase-office-chair/).

* * *

### 5\. Think Office Chair

**2026 Price: $1,099.00 \| [Buy on Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3zpbrbg)**

The Think is an interesting option with a highly flexible backrest and seat pad design similar to the Karman, priced around $1,100. The arms are comparable to the Leap’s and equally comfortable.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/steelcase-think-why-pick.jpg)

In my opinion, the Think is better suited for shorter sitting situations — conference rooms and offices where you won’t spend eight-plus hours in the chair. The lack of padding in the seat and minimal lower support makes me lean toward other options in the lineup for full-day use.

* * *

Today we are going to be taking a close look at one of the most iconic office chairs of the past three decades, the Aeron by Herman Miller. The Aeron has been a bit of a polarizing chair in the office furniture world. Some of its supporters swear by it and will defend its comfort and design until the bitter end. Others haven’t held back in sharing their disdain. We wanted to find out for ourselves how the chair performs and how comfortable it really is.

**Note:** The options included for this review: graphite frame and base, size B, adjustable PostureFit SL, tilt limiter and seat angle, fully adjustable arms, standard arm pads, and 2.5″ carpet casters. The price for an Aeron with these options is $1,750.00.

* * *

### Pros & Cons

#### ✓ Pros

- ✓95/100 build quality – highest tested
- ✓12-year warranty covers everything, 24/7 use
- ✓Three sizes fit 1st-99th percentile
- ✓Arms move with recline – constant positioning
- ✓PostureFit SL – top-5 back comfort tested
- ✓8Z Pellicle mesh – 200k double rub rating

#### ✗ Cons

- ✗No seat depth adjustment
- ✗No armrest width adjustment
- ✗Three sizes needed for a mixed office
- ✗Seat comfort 66/100 – firm, polarizing
- ✗Pronounced side bolsters limit range of motion

**_The Bottom Line:_** _One of the best-built chairs ever tested. Best for users who value longevity, back support, and arm comfort over seat softness. Not ideal if you need a single chair size to fit a diverse group, or if you prefer a softer, more forgiving seat._

### Manufacturer

The Aeron chair is made by Herman Miller. Herman Miller has been in business since 1923 and is one of the oldest and most successful office furniture brands in the world. Originally known as the Michigan Star Furniture Company, it was purchased by De Pree in 1923 and renamed out of respect for his father-in-law, Herman Miller.

Herman Miller has since gone public and expanded to become one of the largest office furniture companies in the world, with factories in the US, UK, Italy and China and a sales presence in over 100 countries. They have also acquired a number of office furniture brands to expand and vertically integrate.

**Country of Origin:** Made in USA

### Return Policy and Warranty

Herman Miller offers a 30-day return policy on the Aeron. If you wish to return your chair, Herman Miller will cover the costs of the return shipment and will give you a full refund. It is recommended that you use the original packaging, but Herman Miller will still work with you on a return if you do not have it.

Herman Miller includes a 12-year warranty on the Aeron chair with no excluded parts. The warranty is valid for 24/7 round-the-clock use. Size A is covered for 300 lbs.; sizes B and C are covered for 350 lbs. If a chair needs to be repaired, the costs will be covered by Herman Miller – they will also send on-site technicians to make repairs, depending on what’s needed and your location. The [Herman Miller warranty](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-warranties/) is one of the best you will find in the entire office industry.

### Shipping and Assembly

The Aeron ships FedEx Ground in a large box weighing around 50 lbs. Herman Miller designed the box with handles cut into the sides to make it easier to move. The chair is packaged with minimal cardboard inside the box – the entire chair is inside a plastic bag to keep it clean. Overall, the chair is well packaged so there is very little chance for damage.

The Aeron arrived at our location fully assembled. The box is designed so that you can open it from the side, roll the chair out, and it is ready for use without any assembly required.

# What is the best office chair for someone over 6Ft tall?

![What is the best office chair for someone over 6Ft tall?](https://crandalloffice.com/cdn/shop/articles/BEST-OFFICE-CHAIRS-FOR-TALL-PEOPLE.png?v=1730947486&width=1600)

Ryan Snyder \|
August 13, 2024

**For someone over 6 feet tall, it’s important to find an office chair that offers proper support, especially for the back, neck, and legs. Here are a few high-end office chairs that are well-suited for taller individuals:**

## **1\. Herman Miller Aeron (Size C):**

• **Key Features:** The Herman Miller Aeron is a classic ergonomic chair, and it comes in three sizes (A, B, and C). Size C is designed for taller and larger individuals, offering a deeper seat and higher backrest.

• **Adjustability:** The Aeron provides excellent lumbar support, adjustable armrests, and a seat that accommodates longer legs. Its PostureFit SL back support system is particularly beneficial for taller users.

• **Comfort:** The mesh material keeps you cool, and the chair’s design promotes good posture, even during long hours of sitting.

### **2\. Steelcase Leap v2:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Leap v2 is highly adjustable, with a flexible backrest that conforms to your movements, ensuring constant support.

• **Adjustability:** The Leap v2 offers a seat depth adjustment, which is crucial for taller users to ensure proper leg support. The backrest height and lumbar support are also adjustable to fit your spine’s natural curve.

• **Comfort:** The Leap v2 is known for its all-day comfort and support, making it a great choice for tall users who spend extended periods seated.

### **3\. Humanscale Freedom Headrest Chair:**

• **Key Features:** Designed by Niels Diffrient, the Humanscale Freedom is an ergonomic chair that automatically adjusts to your posture and movements without manual controls.

• **Adjustability:** The headrest is particularly beneficial for taller individuals, as it adjusts to provide neck and head support when reclining. The seat depth and backrest height adjustments accommodate longer legs and torsos.

• **Comfort:** The Freedom chair’s dynamic recline and minimalist design provide continuous support and reduce strain, making it ideal for taller users.

### **4\. Steelcase Gesture:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Gesture is designed to support a wide range of postures and body types, making it a versatile option for tall individuals.

• **Adjustability:** It features an adjustable seat depth and armrests that move in all directions, ensuring that tall users can find a comfortable and supportive position. The backrest provides excellent lumbar support and adjusts to your posture.

• **Comfort:** The Gesture is praised for its overall comfort and ability to accommodate various sitting styles, which is particularly beneficial for taller users who may need extra space.

### **5\. Haworth Zody:**

• **Key Features:** The Haworth Zody is a highly ergonomic chair with a focus on sustainability and comfort.

• **Adjustability:** It offers seat depth adjustment, lumbar support, and backrest height adjustment, all of which are crucial for taller users. The Zody’s pelvic support system also helps maintain good posture.

• **Comfort:** The Zody is designed to provide personalized support, making it a comfortable choice for taller users who need a chair that adapts to their body.

### **6\. Knoll ReGeneration:**

• **Key Features:** The Knoll ReGeneration is a modern ergonomic chair that supports active sitting, making it a great option for those who move frequently throughout the day.

• **Adjustability:** It offers seat depth adjustment, lumbar support, and flexible armrests that adapt to various postures. The chair’s design accommodates taller users by providing ample seat depth and a supportive backrest.

• **Comfort:** The ReGeneration’s flexible design and supportive mesh back make it a comfortable option for taller individuals who need a chair that moves with them.

### **Considerations for Tall Users:**

• **Seat Depth:** Ensure the chair has a deep enough seat to support your thighs without cutting off circulation.

• **Backrest Height:** Look for chairs with adjustable or tall backrests to provide adequate support for your upper back and shoulders.

• **Lumbar Support:** Adjustable lumbar support is crucial for maintaining good posture, especially for taller users who may need the support higher up on the backrest.

# Office Chair Depth and Seat Size Comparison: What Works for Your Body Type?

2025-09-25

When most people think about buying an office chair, the first things that come to mind are style, brand, or maybe the price tag. But if you’ve ever sat in a chair that felt “off” even though it looked comfortable, chances are the problem was with the seat depth or chair size.

The ergonomic chair seat depth and overall office chair size directly affect your posture, circulation, and long-term comfort. A chair that’s too deep may leave shorter users with dangling feet or pressure behind the knees, while a chair that’s too shallow won’t provide enough thigh support for taller individuals. Similarly, seat width and overall chair size must align with your body type to prevent discomfort or poor posture.

In this guide, we’ll compare office chair depth and seat size, explain why they matter, and show you how to find the best chair for your body type. Whether you’re petite, tall, or somewhere in between, the right seat dimensions can make a world of difference in your daily comfort and productivity.

**Understanding Ergonomic Chair Seat Depth**

Seat depth refers to the distance between the backrest of the chair and the front edge of the seat. It might sound like a small detail, but it’s one of the most important factors in determining how well your chair supports your body.

Time and again we get asked the same question…. _“what is the correct ergonomic height setting for my office chair?”_ The answer is not that simple because it depends on two main factors, namely **your height**, and the **type of work** that you do. Because every person and their job environment is unique, the correct height for your desk, monitor and office chair will fall within a range of values. ### Summary

> The correct office chair height is when your feet are flat on the floor, your knees are slightly below the level of your hips, and your elbows are bent at approximately 90° and can rest comfortably on the arm pads. Once your chair has been correctly adjusted, raise or lower your desk so that the desk surface is level with the top of the armrests.

![correct desk height for office chairs](https://karo.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/desk-dimensions-768x445.jpg.webp)

Whether you are standing or sitting, adjust the desk, office chair and monitor so that it is at a comfortable ergonomic height. [Best practices for ergonomics in the workplace](https://karo.co.za/knowledge-center/ergonomics-in-the-workplace/). Find out whether [it is good to alternate between sitting and standing at work](https://karo.co.za/knowledge-center/standing-desk/).

Affiliate Disclaimer: We independently review everything we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Three years ago, we first brought the [Steelcase Leap V2](https://www.btod.com/steelcase-leap-v2) to BTOD.com for review. Since that time, it has consistently ranked at the top of our [list of best office chairs](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-reviews/).

### Pros & Cons

#### Pros

- ✅ Best-in-class 4-way adjustable arms
- ✅ Exceptional seat back flexibility and lumbar support
- ✅ Fits users 5’2″–6’6″ with wide height range
- ✅ Proven long-term build quality — chairs from 2006 still functional
- ✅ Five tilt limit settings for flexible recline control
- ✅ Seat slider accommodates a wide range of leg lengths

#### Cons

- ❌ Seat pad too thin for some users
- ❌ Headrest pushes head forward — not worth the $180 add-on for most
- ❌ Headrest tends to drop from set position over time
- ❌ Return policy shortened from 30 days to 14 days on Steelcase.com
- ❌ New chair price has risen significantly over the years

**_The Bottom Line:_** _The Leap V2 remains one of the best ergonomic chairs on the market three years in, but the thin seat pad might not be the best option if you prefer a thick padded seat._

* * *

### 1\. Price

The price of the chair has changed since we first brought it into our office. With 4-way adjustable arms, height-adjustable lumbar support, and standard casters — the configuration we recommend — the Leap V2 now retails for [around $1,399 on the Steelcase website](https://bit.ly/3PS3KB9). Alternatively, you can purchase a [fully refurbished Steelcase Leap for $640.99 at BTOD](https://www.btod.com/steelcase-leap-v2) — about half the price of new.

![Steelcase Leap V2 price 2026](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/steelcase-leap-price-2026.jpg)

* * *

### 2\. Steelcase Policies

Some of the policies on the Steelcase website have changed, specifically the return and warranty policies. The return policy has gone from 30 days down to 14, and the warranty for sales outside of North America has changed — so it’s worth taking a closer look at the fine print before ordering directly from Steelcase.

* * *

### 3\. Leap Build Quality

When you spend this much on an office chair, you want to know it will hold up. I do believe that the Leap V2 has the build quality you would expect. Not only have I experienced this personally, but at BTOD, [we refurbish thousands of used Leap V2 chairs dating back to 2006](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcase-leap-refurbished/). While some come in rough shape, the functionality is almost always intact, usually we just tighten things up and clean the upholstery. Overall, this chair has one of the best build qualities on the market.

![Great quality chair](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-4.jpg)Great quality chair

* * *

### 4\. Leap Adjustments

One of the reasons the Leap V2 consistently ranks as a great chair for most people is how adjustable it is. The seat height drops to 15.5″ and raises to 20.5″, fitting users roughly 5’2″ to 6’6″ tall. A seat slider adjusts the depth of the seat pan to accommodate different leg lengths. The tilt limiter offers five settings to control how far back you can recline, and tilt tension lets you dial in how much effort it takes to lean back.

![Making adjustments](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-5.jpg)Making adjustments

Steelcase offers three arm options: no arms, height-adjustable only, and 4-way adjustable. We strongly recommend the 4-way arms as they’re probably my favorite armrests overall. Height, width, depth, and pivot are all adjustable, giving almost anyone the ability to find a comfortable position. These arms are a genuine differentiator for the Leap.

* * *

### 5\. Seat Back

One of my favorite components of the Leap V2 is the seat back. It’s one of the best in the business for lumbar support. The side knob lets you adjust lumbar tension significantly, and you can really feel the difference in the lower back. If you want less pronounced support, dial it down; if you like firm support, ratchet it up. The lumbar support is also height-adjustable for precise positioning. As a side note, our VP Ryan didn’t initially like the lumbar feel — he simply removed the support entirely and now loves the chair. That kind of flexibility is rare.

![The seat back is comfortable](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-7.jpg)The seat back is comfortable

* * *

### 6\. Leap Headrest

Personally, I dislike the headrest on the Leap V2 and that’s been true since the first time I sat in the chair. It doesn’t provide the support I’m looking for and actually feels like it pushes my head forward. The only time I marginally appreciate it is in a deeply reclined position. The headrest also has a tendency to slip from where it’s set over time. At $180 as an add-on, I wouldn’t recommend it unless you’ve tried it and know it works for your body.

![The headrest on the chair](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-8.jpg)The headrest on the chair

* * *

### 7\. Leap Comfort

Build quality and adjustments only matter if the chair is actually comfortable and fortunately the Leap V2 delivers. The seat has a concave design that molds around you, and the flexible waterfall front edge prevents you from feeling locked in. Press on the sides or front of the seat and you’ll see that it flexes meaningfully. This allows you to move throughout the day and promotes better blood flow to the legs.

![Thin seat pad](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-9.jpg)Thin seat pad

That said, the seat pad is thin — and by design. Many high-end chairs use thinner seat

# Steelcase Gesture Office Chair Review for 2026

[Greg Knighton](https://www.btod.com/blog/author/greg/)
17 May 2026 [Product Reviews](https://www.btod.com/blog/category/product-reviews/)[4 Comments](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcase-gesture-chair-review/#comments)

Affiliate Disclaimer: We independently review everything we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

If you’re looking for an ergonomic chair that will best fit a wide range of users out of the box, the [Steelcase Gesture](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcase-leap-3-years-later/) is likely what you need. With our highest scope of users score at 91, our closest competitor scored seven points less and was a close family member, the Steelcase Leap.

Steelcase Gesture Office Chair Review - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[Steelcase Gesture Office Chair Review](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=czO9SnFEd1s) [BTODtv](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCDJZPusVYgqWwP67JnZviRw)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/mfL2IRHF27rhr4J_-_ZzqxEST7eUWtQBYoYzofpAhKNHsoX_jP9xJEzv3-mVOWj0V1-H8YThBg=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

BTODtv96.7K subscribers

[Watch on](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=czO9SnFEd1s)

Of course, this doesn’t come without a cost. At $1,499+, the Steelcase Gesture is one of the most expensive chairs we tested. Let’s take a closer look to find out if it’s worth the price tag.

* * *

### Pros & Cons

| ✓ Pros | ✗ Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✓ 91/100 scope of users , widest range of any chair tested | ✗ No back-height adjustment |
| ✓ 4-way arms with 10.25″-22.5″ width range, unmatched | ✗ Back doesn’t fully lock upright (slight flex remains) |
| ✓ Intuitive seat slider knob (no awkward butt-slide required) | ✗ $1,499+ starting price is high |
| ✓ Ships fully assembled | ✗ Made in Mexico, not USA |
| ✓ 400 lb. 24/7 capacity, lifetime frame warranty |  |

* * *

**_The Bottom Line:_** _After several weeks in the Gesture, I can say it lives up to the score. It’s tied with the Leap for our best overall chair. If you need a chair that fits the widest range of users possible, the Gesture is the one I’d point you to. The arms alone are worth the attention._

* * *

* * *

### Manufacturer

Steelcase was established in 1912 as the Metal Office Furniture Company. By 1954, its name changed to Steelcase Inc. and by 1998 it became a publicly traded company. Today it is one of the largest office furniture manufacturers in the world.

### Steelcase Gesture History

The development of the Gesture was as unique as the chair itself, starting first with studying the human body. Steelcase studied over 2,000 people from around the globe to understand posture. Through this research, they found that new technology created nine additional postures that existing seating wasn’t addressing. The Gesture Chair was created to address all of them.

### Country of Origin / Specifications

**Made in Mexico**

- **Seat Height:** 16″-20.5″ \| **Seat Depth:** 15.75″-18.75″ \| **Seat Width:** 19.25″
- **Arm Height:** 7.25″-11.5″ \| **Arm Width:** 10.25″-22.5″
- **Back Height/Width:** 24.0625″ H / 16.25″ W \| **Weight Rating:** 400 lbs.
- **Overall:** 24.75″ D x 27″ W x 38.5″-43.5″ H

**Features:** Seat height, seat depth, 4D arms (massive range), 3-position tilt lock, optional adjustable lumbar, flexible backrest, 400 lb. capacity.

**2026 Starting Price: $1,499.00** \| Where to buy: [Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3JpRhm8)

* * *

### Return Policy

All Steelcase chairs come with a 30-day money back guarantee, including free return shipping with no restocking fees. The chair must be returned in new condition in the original packaging to receive the full refund.

### Warranty

The Gesture includes one of the best warranties in the business. The frame is covered for the lifetime of the original owner. Mechanisms, gas cylinders, arms, foam padding, and casters are covered for 12 years. Valid for 24/7 usage regardless of shift. Steelcase will repair or replace your chair at no charge.

* * *

### Shipping

When ordered in small quantities, the Gesture ships via FedEx Ground in a large box with handles, weighing approximately 70 lbs. You may want an extra set of hands to move it.

### Assembly

One of the things I really like about the Gesture is that it ships fully assembled. The only thing required is removing the chair from the box and pulling away the minimal packaging.

* * *

### Build Quality (88/100)

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/gesture-build-quality-back-quartering.jpg)

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/gesture-build-quality-mechanism.jpg)

With a score of 88/100, the Gesture ranked fourth out of all chairs tested. The only chair to outrank it was the [iconic Aeron chair, scoring a 95](https://www.btod.com/blog/herman-miller-aeron-review/). The Steelcase Gesture was one of the most well put together chairs we tested. From the bottom of the chair to the top of the backrest, there was a high level of quality and consistency throughout. Like the Steelcase Leap, the Gesture uses quite a few plastic components. Don’t let this fool you though: the chair is solid and well built. Most plastic components were either used for flexibility in the chair back or to cover metal components. Where the Gesture scored an additional point over the Leap was how they finished the bottom of the seat. Specifically, how they used custom molded plastic to cover the metal mechanism components, creating a cleaner look.

* * *

### Scope of Users (91/100)

If you’re looking for a single chair that is adjustable enough to fit most users, the Gesture is by far the best I’ve tested. The seat height adjustment at 16″-21″ fits the 5th to 95th percentile without issues. Pair that with a seat slider for shorter and longer legs, and you shouldn’t have issues getting comfortable. Their secret to maximizing the user score is in the arms. While a lot of arms include 4-way adjustment, none offered the range of motion found on the Gesture. With 10.25″ to 22.5″ of width adjustment paired with height, depth, and pivot, all typing and working positions should be supported properly. The Gesture also features a 400 lb. weight rating. For a comparison of how the Gesture fits against the Leap in adjustability, see our [Steelcase Leap vs. Gesture comparison](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcasae-leap-vs-gesture-chair/).

* * *

### Seat Comfort (81/100)

# Herman Miller Aeron VS. Steelcase Gesture Chair in 2026

[Ryan Bald](https://www.btod.com/blog/author/ryan/)
14 May 2026 [Product Comparisons](https://www.btod.com/blog/category/comparisons/)[Leave a comment](https://www.btod.com/blog/aeron-chair-vs-gesture-chair/#respond)

Affiliate Disclaimer: We independently review everything we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

This comparison is going to feature old school vs. new school chair ergonomics. The [Aeron was the gold standard](https://www.btod.com/blog/herman-miller-aeron-review/) in chair ergonomics when it was released in 1994, but a lot has changed since then.

Steelcase Gesture vs Herman Miller Aeron \| Office Chair Tier List - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[Steelcase Gesture vs Herman Miller Aeron \| Office Chair Tier List](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BDzk_KWA-w0) [moreBTODtv](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UChycULQ_WBOCrrdUgo-eCEQ)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/ytc/AIdro_m1EEJmb4AB8E_nD2eq-iMSjmxR3lNZovQx_YA7vAqDi3v7-00Cbm8bWsbU_5uzAC5PLA=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

moreBTODtv330 subscribers

[Watch on](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BDzk_KWA-w0)

How does the Aeron stack up against a high-end rival chair from their biggest competitor? Steelcase [developed the Gesture](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcase-gesture-chair-review/), which is currently one of their most high-end ergonomic chairs. It was designed with all the bells and whistles you can expect from Steelcase but it takes a lot to go up against the iconic Aeron. How will these chairs compare and which one is the right choice for you? Let’s find out!

* * *

### Head-to-Head Comparison

| Category | Steelcase Gesture | Herman Miller Aeron |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starting Price | $1,499 | $1,835 |
| Build Quality | More plastic, very high quality | Aluminum + mesh, lightest chair we’ve tested |
| Seat Comfort | Foam pad, universally comfortable | Mesh only, firm, polarizing |
| Back Support | Flexible high back, adjustable lumbar | PostureFit SL lumbar, mid back |
| Armrests | Widest range we’ve tested, 4-way | Thick, squishy pads, no width adjust |
| Fits Who | One size fits most | Three sizes (A, B, C) required |
| Adjustability | Seat slider + arm width | Forward seat tilt |
| Weight Capacity | 400 lbs. | 350 lbs. |
| Upholstery | Fabric or leather, 70+ colors | Mesh only, 3 colors |
| Warranty | 12 years, 24/7 | 12 years, 24/7 |

**_The Bottom Line:_** _The Gesture wins on paper in most categories, but the Aeron wins on feel. If you hate mesh seats or need a fabric option, the Gesture is the easy choice. If you want the best recline and the best arm pads, get the Aeron._

* * *

### Specs

One big difference between the Aeron and Gesture is that the Aeron was designed with different size options, while the Gesture is available in one size only. The Aeron is available in 3 sizes: A, B and C. A is small, B is medium and C is large. Size B is the most commonly chosen chair and it was the model we used for testing.

|  | Gesture | Aeron (size B) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manufacturer | Steelcase | Herman Miller |
| Country of Origin | Mexico | USA |
| Overall Dimensions | 23.75″D x 27″W x 38.5-43.5″H | 27″D x 27″W x 36.5-41″H |
| Seat Height Range | 16″ – 21″ | 16″ – 20.5″ |
| Base Dimensions | 26″ Diameter | 27″ Diameter |
| Seat Dimensions | 20″W x 15.75-18.5″D | 17″W x 16.75″D |
| Back Dimensions | 16.25″W x 24″H | 21.5″W x 22″H |
| Distance Between Arms | 10.25-22.5″ | 17″ |
| Arm Height from Seat | 7.25-11.5″ | 5.5-9.75″ |
| Weight Capacity | 400 lbs. | 350 lbs. |
| Chair Weight | 61 lbs. | 41 lbs. |
| Shipping Weight | 78 lbs. | 46 lbs. |
| Shipping Dimensions | 23.5″ x 29″ x 44.5″ | 41″ x 28″ x 27″ |

* * *

### 2026 Pricing

The Aeron has a lower starting price than the Gesture. This is because Herman Miller allows you to order the Aeron with your choice of adjustability. You can add things like adjustable arms, tilt lock positions and lumbar support. If you order the most basic Aeron, then you can get it for $1,400.00. But, upgrading to the most adjustable version will bring the price up to $1,875.00. There are also options to upgrade the mesh and finish options. We will go more in-depth on those features in the Upholstery and Finish sections below.

The Gesture has a starting price of $1,499.99 but the Gesture comes standard with fully adjustable arms, lumbar support, tilt lock and a seat slider. You can also upgrade the upholstery and finish on the Gesture, which we will address in the Upholstery and Finish sections below.

|  | Gesture | Aeron |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starting Price | $1,499.00 | $1,835.00 |
| Where To Buy | [Buy Gesture on Steelcase.com](https://www.steelcase.com/products/office-chairs/gesture/) | [Buy Aeron on HermanMiller.com](https://bit.ly/3vvtGts) |

* * *

### Return Policy

Steelcase and Herman Miller both have great return policies. Steelcase allows you to return the Gesture within the first 30 days for a full refund. Steelcase will cover the return shipping costs. The only requirements from Steelcase are that you ship the Gesture back in the original packaging and it must arrive back in like new condition.

Herman Miller also gives you 30 days to return the Aeron for a full refund. You cover your return shipping costs of $99. Herman Miller does require that the Aeron is returned in like new condition, and they do not require the original packaging. If you no longer have the box, reach out to Herman Miller and they will help you facilitate a return. This will come at a cost of 10% restocking fees.

### Warranty

In my opinion, Herman Miller and Steelcase have the [two best office chair warranties](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-warranties/) in the industry. Their warranties are very similar, but they do have a couple of differences. The Gesture and Aeron are both covered for 12 years and have no excluded components. Both warranties are valid for 24/7 usage. The Aeron is covered for people that are 300-350 lbs., depending on the size you order. The Gesture is covered for people weighing up to 400 lbs.

[![Four Great Ergo Chairs for Tall Users](https://cdn11.bigcommerce.com/s-492apnl0xy/images/stencil/300x300/uploaded_images/four-great-ergo-chairs-for-tall-users-thumb.jpg?t=1488234208)](https://www.thehumansolution.com/blog/four-great-ergo-chairs-for-tall-users/)

![](https://www.thehumansolution.com/product_images/uploaded_images/four-great-ergo-chairs-for-tall-users-main.jpg)

If you are a very tall person, or even just a little taller than average, there is no doubt that you have experienced the discomfort and lack of support that comes from sitting all day in a one size fits all office chair. You can adjust one of those cookie-cutter, big-box office store chairs only so high, after all, and if it’s not high enough, you have no real options for getting comfortable. We offer a large selection of chairs that work well for tall or very tall users. We even have a whole section on our website with
[recommended chairs for tall people](http://www.thehumansolution.com/tall-office-chair.html), however, to get you started; I've compiled this list of four recommended chairs that work great for taller users.

**The Ergonomic Chair for the Mobile Generation**

Though it may not be classified specifically as a “tall” chair, the
[Steelcase Gesture Chair](http://www.thehumansolution.com/steelcase-gesture-chair-build-your-own.html) is the chair that's so versatile, this could probably be featured on just about any list of the “best” ergo chairs for specific situations.  The arm rests are some of the most adjustable I've ever seen; they can be widened to 22.5” wide, and at their tallest point, they are nearly 10” above the seat cushion. The Steelcase Gesture can also be ordered with a taller cylinder option, which will allow the user to raise the seat up to 22.5”, and it comes standard with a seat slider to increase the seat depth for longer legs. This chair is so flexible, users of almost any height can easily find a comfortable position whether working on a PC, tablet, phone or other device.

**The Cadillac of Chairs**

For the height in customization and comfort, check out the
[BodyBilt Extra Tall “Stretch” Chair](http://www.thehumansolution.com/bodybilt-2509-3509-stretch-tall-ergonomic-chair.html), either with a headrest or not. Either way, you’ll get an extra high backrest for maximum support, an extra long seat pan and a tall cylinder, with over 5” of height adjustment. If you do decide to add a headrest, the unique and highly adjustable “Fore-aft neckroll” offers two pivot points to adjust the angle and a 4” height range. You can even flip this headrest out of the way when you don’t want to use it. As with all BodyBilt chairs, the Extra Tall “Stretch” edition can be ordered with a host of customizable ergonomic features, like an extra layer of memory foam on the seat and back cushions and multiple options for the lumbar support and arm rests. When you order a BodyBilt chair, you are getting top of the line comfort and customization, built just for you.

**The Tall Chair on a Budget**

Need something with customizable options for a tall user, but also need to stay within a budget? Several chairs available by ergoCentric can be configured with “tall” options.  The
[ergoCentric airCentric](http://www.thehumansolution.com/ergocentric-aircentric-air-flow-ergonomic-chair.html) and [myCentric](http://www.thehumansolution.com/ergocentric-mycentric-ergonomic-office-chair.html) chairs can be ordered with customized features like an extra long seat and a taller cylinder for seat height adjustment. The [ergoCentric geoCentric](http://www.thehumansolution.com/ergocentric-geocentric-series-task-chairs.html) has either an extra tall or an extra high backrest option, with additional neck support. You can even add additional air lumbar support, which is adjustable. Even with all of the added “tall” features, these ergoCentric chairs come in at a price point that is about half what you’ll pay for many other ergonomic chairs.

**The Most Popular**

Like the Gesture chair, the
[Ergohuman chair](http://www.thehumansolution.com/ergohuman1.html) is not specifically classified as a “tall” chair. However, with a seat that can be adjusted as high as about 23” and an adjustable seat depth, this chair easily accommodates a taller than average user as is. The Ergohuman chair is available upholstered in either mesh or leather, or you can choose a leather seat and mesh back. Finally, choose whether you want a headrest or not, and you’re done. The Ergohuman chair is one of the most popular ergonomic chairs in the world, a favorite of large businesses, government agencies and home office users alike.

_For many more ergonomic chair recommendations, visit us at [TheHumanSolution.com](http://www.thehumansolution.com/)!_

# What is the best office chair for someone over 6Ft tall?

![What is the best office chair for someone over 6Ft tall?](https://crandalloffice.com/cdn/shop/articles/BEST-OFFICE-CHAIRS-FOR-TALL-PEOPLE.png?v=1730947486&width=1600)

Ryan Snyder \|
August 13, 2024

**For someone over 6 feet tall, it’s important to find an office chair that offers proper support, especially for the back, neck, and legs. Here are a few high-end office chairs that are well-suited for taller individuals:**

## **1\. Herman Miller Aeron (Size C):**

• **Key Features:** The Herman Miller Aeron is a classic ergonomic chair, and it comes in three sizes (A, B, and C). Size C is designed for taller and larger individuals, offering a deeper seat and higher backrest.

• **Adjustability:** The Aeron provides excellent lumbar support, adjustable armrests, and a seat that accommodates longer legs. Its PostureFit SL back support system is particularly beneficial for taller users.

• **Comfort:** The mesh material keeps you cool, and the chair’s design promotes good posture, even during long hours of sitting.

### **2\. Steelcase Leap v2:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Leap v2 is highly adjustable, with a flexible backrest that conforms to your movements, ensuring constant support.

• **Adjustability:** The Leap v2 offers a seat depth adjustment, which is crucial for taller users to ensure proper leg support. The backrest height and lumbar support are also adjustable to fit your spine’s natural curve.

• **Comfort:** The Leap v2 is known for its all-day comfort and support, making it a great choice for tall users who spend extended periods seated.

### **3\. Humanscale Freedom Headrest Chair:**

• **Key Features:** Designed by Niels Diffrient, the Humanscale Freedom is an ergonomic chair that automatically adjusts to your posture and movements without manual controls.

• **Adjustability:** The headrest is particularly beneficial for taller individuals, as it adjusts to provide neck and head support when reclining. The seat depth and backrest height adjustments accommodate longer legs and torsos.

• **Comfort:** The Freedom chair’s dynamic recline and minimalist design provide continuous support and reduce strain, making it ideal for taller users.

### **4\. Steelcase Gesture:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Gesture is designed to support a wide range of postures and body types, making it a versatile option for tall individuals.

• **Adjustability:** It features an adjustable seat depth and armrests that move in all directions, ensuring that tall users can find a comfortable and supportive position. The backrest provides excellent lumbar support and adjusts to your posture.

• **Comfort:** The Gesture is praised for its overall comfort and ability to accommodate various sitting styles, which is particularly beneficial for taller users who may need extra space.

### **5\. Haworth Zody:**

• **Key Features:** The Haworth Zody is a highly ergonomic chair with a focus on sustainability and comfort.

• **Adjustability:** It offers seat depth adjustment, lumbar support, and backrest height adjustment, all of which are crucial for taller users. The Zody’s pelvic support system also helps maintain good posture.

• **Comfort:** The Zody is designed to provide personalized support, making it a comfortable choice for taller users who need a chair that adapts to their body.

### **6\. Knoll ReGeneration:**

• **Key Features:** The Knoll ReGeneration is a modern ergonomic chair that supports active sitting, making it a great option for those who move frequently throughout the day.

• **Adjustability:** It offers seat depth adjustment, lumbar support, and flexible armrests that adapt to various postures. The chair’s design accommodates taller users by providing ample seat depth and a supportive backrest.

• **Comfort:** The ReGeneration’s flexible design and supportive mesh back make it a comfortable option for taller individuals who need a chair that moves with them.

### **Considerations for Tall Users:**

• **Seat Depth:** Ensure the chair has a deep enough seat to support your thighs without cutting off circulation.

• **Backrest Height:** Look for chairs with adjustable or tall backrests to provide adequate support for your upper back and shoulders.

• **Lumbar Support:** Adjustable lumbar support is crucial for maintaining good posture, especially for taller users who may need the support higher up on the backrest.

* * *

### Manufacturer

Steelcase was established in 1912 as the Metal Office Furniture Company. By 1954, its name changed to Steelcase Inc. and by 1998 it became a publicly traded company. Today it is one of the largest office furniture manufacturers in the world.

### Steelcase Gesture History

The development of the Gesture was as unique as the chair itself, starting first with studying the human body. Steelcase studied over 2,000 people from around the globe to understand posture. Through this research, they found that new technology created nine additional postures that existing seating wasn’t addressing. The Gesture Chair was created to address all of them.

### Country of Origin / Specifications

**Made in Mexico**

- **Seat Height:** 16″-20.5″ \| **Seat Depth:** 15.75″-18.75″ \| **Seat Width:** 19.25″
- **Arm Height:** 7.25″-11.5″ \| **Arm Width:** 10.25″-22.5″
- **Back Height/Width:** 24.0625″ H / 16.25″ W \| **Weight Rating:** 400 lbs.
- **Overall:** 24.75″ D x 27″ W x 38.5″-43.5″ H

**Features:** Seat height, seat depth, 4D arms (massive range), 3-position tilt lock, optional adjustable lumbar, flexible backrest, 400 lb. capacity.

**2026 Starting Price: $1,499.00** \| Where to buy: [Steelcase.com](https://bit.ly/3JpRhm8)

* * *

### Return Policy

All Steelcase chairs come with a 30-day money back guarantee, including free return shipping with no restocking fees. The chair must be returned in new condition in the original packaging to receive the full refund.

### Warranty

The Gesture includes one of the best warranties in the business. The frame is covered for the lifetime of the original owner. Mechanisms, gas cylinders, arms, foam padding, and casters are covered for 12 years. Valid for 24/7 usage regardless of shift. Steelcase will repair or replace your chair at no charge.

* * *

### Shipping

When ordered in small quantities, the Gesture ships via FedEx Ground in a large box with handles, weighing approximately 70 lbs. You may want an extra set of hands to move it.

### Assembly

One of the things I really like about the Gesture is that it ships fully assembled. The only thing required is removing the chair from the box and pulling away the minimal packaging.

* * *

### Build Quality (88/100)

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/gesture-build-quality-back-quartering.jpg)

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/gesture-build-quality-mechanism.jpg)

With a score of 88/100, the Gesture ranked fourth out of all chairs tested. The only chair to outrank it was the [iconic Aeron chair, scoring a 95](https://www.btod.com/blog/herman-miller-aeron-review/). The Steelcase Gesture was one of the most well put together chairs we tested. From the bottom of the chair to the top of the backrest, there was a high level of quality and consistency throughout. Like the Steelcase Leap, the Gesture uses quite a few plastic components. Don’t let this fool you though: the chair is solid and well built. Most plastic components were either used for flexibility in the chair back or to cover metal components. Where the Gesture scored an additional point over the Leap was how they finished the bottom of the seat. Specifically, how they used custom molded plastic to cover the metal mechanism components, creating a cleaner look.

* * *

### Scope of Users (91/100)

If you’re looking for a single chair that is adjustable enough to fit most users, the Gesture is by far the best I’ve tested. The seat height adjustment at 16″-21″ fits the 5th to 95th percentile without issues. Pair that with a seat slider for shorter and longer legs, and you shouldn’t have issues getting comfortable. Their secret to maximizing the user score is in the arms. While a lot of arms include 4-way adjustment, none offered the range of motion found on the Gesture. With 10.25″ to 22.5″ of width adjustment paired with height, depth, and pivot, all typing and working positions should be supported properly. The Gesture also features a 400 lb. weight rating. For a comparison of how the Gesture fits against the Leap in adjustability, see our [Steelcase Leap vs. Gesture comparison](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcasae-leap-vs-gesture-chair/).

* * *

### Seat Comfort (81/100)

• **Key Features:** The Herman Miller Aeron is a classic ergonomic chair, and it comes in three sizes (A, B, and C). Size C is designed for taller and larger individuals, offering a deeper seat and higher backrest.

### **2\. Steelcase Leap v2:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Leap v2 is highly adjustable, with a flexible backrest that conforms to your movements, ensuring constant support.

• **Adjustability:** The Leap v2 offers a seat depth adjustment, which is crucial for taller users to ensure proper leg support. The backrest height and lumbar support are also adjustable to fit your spine’s natural curve.

• **Comfort:** The Leap v2 is known for its all-day comfort and support, making it a great choice for tall users who spend extended periods seated.

### **3\. Humanscale Freedom Headrest Chair:**

• **Key Features:** Designed by Niels Diffrient, the Humanscale Freedom is an ergonomic chair that automatically adjusts to your posture and movements without manual controls.

• **Adjustability:** The headrest is particularly beneficial for taller individuals, as it adjusts to provide neck and head support when reclining. The seat depth and backrest height adjustments accommodate longer legs and torsos.

• **Comfort:** The Freedom chair’s dynamic recline and minimalist design provide continuous support and reduce strain, making it ideal for taller users.

### **4\. Steelcase Gesture:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Gesture is designed to support a wide range of postures and body types, making it a versatile option for tall individuals.

• **Adjustability:** It features an adjustable seat depth and armrests that move in all directions, ensuring that tall users can find a comfortable and supportive position. The backrest provides excellent lumbar support and adjusts to your posture.

• **Comfort:** The Gesture is praised for its overall comfort and ability to accommodate various sitting styles, which is particularly beneficial for taller users who may need extra space.

### **5\. Haworth Zody:**

• **Key Features:** The Haworth Zody is a highly ergonomic chair with a focus on sustainability and comfort.

### **6\. Knoll ReGeneration:**

• **Key Features:** The Knoll ReGeneration is a modern ergonomic chair that supports active sitting, making it a great option for those who move frequently throughout the day.

• **Seat Depth:** Ensure the chair has a deep enough seat to support your thighs without cutting off circulation.

Herman Miller has since gone public and expanded to become one of the largest office furniture companies in the world, with factories in the US, UK, Italy and China and a sales presence in over 100 countries. Size A is covered for 300 lbs.; sizes B and C are covered for 350 lbs. If a chair needs to be repaired, the costs will be covered by Herman Miller – they will also send on-site technicians to make repairs, depending on what’s needed and your location. ### Aeron Armrests

![Arm pivot](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/aeron-armrest-pivot.jpg)

If you get the [fully adjustable arms](https://www.btod.com/blog/4-office-chair-armrest-adjustments/), which we recommend, you’re going to get three-way adjustments. Height, depth, and pivot adjustments all have a very wide range, allowing you to move and rest your arms in your preferred position. While the arms don’t provide width adjustment, the pivot adjustment makes up for it with range and movements that act as width adjustment.

![Lowest arm height and tallest height shown](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/aeron-armrest-heights.jpg)Herman Miller Aeron Chairs Worth It?

The arm caps themselves are very soft and comfortable to rest your arms on. Throughout our chair testing, they may be some of the most comfortable arm caps we’ve used.

![Pressing thumb into arm pad](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/aeron-armrest-closeup-and-padding.jpg)Why Herman Miller Chairs Are Good

### Aeron Chair Back Support

The Aeron chair is also known for providing a few different options to choose from for [solid lumbar support](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-reviews/). First, there is a no lumbar option, utilizing just the support from the natural curve of the backrest. You can also get a height-adjustable lumbar system or the Posture Fit SL, which covers a larger portion of your back and gives you depth control to the lumbar adjustment. Overall, the Aeron provides good back support, scoring well from almost all the testers in our office, so you can expect to have good support with this chair.

![Aeron's backrest while seated](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/aeron-backrest-comfort-side-view-sitting.jpg)

### Aeron Forward Seat Tilt

One added bonus that this chair has that a lot of others don’t, is forward seat tilt. This specific adjustment isn’t used in a ton of applications, but there are people that are specifically looking for forward seat tilt. If you’re looking for a high-end chair with that option, this may be the chair for you.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/aeron-ergonomics-upright-to-forward-tilt.jpg)

###### Aeron Recline Function

The Aeron has a recline function that almost feels like a hybrid between a knee tilt and synchro tilt mechanism that is maybe the most smooth adjustment that there is on an office chair. It’s similar to a rocking feeling, but it’s very easy to get yourself back upright to the full upright sitting position. It has very nice tension adjustment and multiple locking positions, making it overall a great chair for those who like to rock or recline throughout the day.

![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/aeron-ergonomics-tilt-locks-recline-upright.jpg)

# What I Think About the Steelcase Leap V2 3 Years Later

Affiliate Disclaimer: We independently review everything we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Three years ago, we first brought the [Steelcase Leap V2](https://www.btod.com/steelcase-leap-v2) to BTOD.com for review. Since that time, it has consistently ranked at the top of our [list of best office chairs](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-reviews/).

Steelcase Leap v2 Review: My Opinion 3 Years Later - YouTube

[Steelcase Leap v2 Review: My Opinion 3 Years Later](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iaZPWPqCsIo) [BTODtv](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCDJZPusVYgqWwP67JnZviRw)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/mfL2IRHF27rhr4J_-_ZzqxEST7eUWtQBYoYzofpAhKNHsoX_jP9xJEzv3-mVOWj0V1-H8YThBg=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

It’s also been the chair I have been personally using as my daily driver. After three years in the chair, some of my opinions have changed from that initial review. Here’s what I think now.

* * *

Full Disclaimer: We are an office furniture dealer and sell some of the Steelcase chairs we review. * * *

### Pros & Cons

#### Pros

- ✅ Best-in-class 4-way adjustable arms
- ✅ Exceptional seat back flexibility and lumbar support
- ✅ Fits users 5’2″–6’6″ with wide height range
- ✅ Proven long-term build quality — chairs from 2006 still functional
- ✅ Five tilt limit settings for flexible recline control
- ✅ Seat slider accommodates a wide range of leg lengths

#### Cons

- ❌ Seat pad too thin for some users
- ❌ Headrest pushes head forward — not worth the $180 add-on for most
- ❌ Headrest tends to drop from set position over time
- ❌ Return policy shortened from 30 days to 14 days on Steelcase.com
- ❌ New chair price has risen significantly over the years

**_The Bottom Line:_** _The Leap V2 remains one of the best ergonomic chairs on the market three years in, but the thin seat pad might not be the best option if you prefer a thick padded seat._

[![](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/office-chair-guide-blog-768x120px-1.jpg)](https://www.btod.com/chairlist/)

* * *

### 1\. Price

The price of the chair has changed since we first brought it into our office. With 4-way adjustable arms, height-adjustable lumbar support, and standard casters — the configuration we recommend — the Leap V2 now retails for [around $1,399 on the Steelcase website](https://bit.ly/3PS3KB9). Alternatively, you can purchase a [fully refurbished Steelcase Leap for $640.99 at BTOD](https://www.btod.com/steelcase-leap-v2) — about half the price of new.

![Steelcase Leap V2 price 2026](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/steelcase-leap-price-2026.jpg)

* * *

### 2\. Steelcase Policies

Some of the policies on the Steelcase website have changed, specifically the return and warranty policies. The return policy has gone from 30 days down to 14, and the warranty for sales outside of North America has changed — so it’s worth taking a closer look at the fine print before ordering directly from Steelcase.

* * *

### 3\. Leap Build Quality

When you spend this much on an office chair, you want to know it will hold up. I do believe that the Leap V2 has the build quality you would expect. Not only have I experienced this personally, but at BTOD, [we refurbish thousands of used Leap V2 chairs dating back to 2006](https://www.btod.com/blog/steelcase-leap-refurbished/). While some come in rough shape, the functionality is almost always intact, usually we just tighten things up and clean the upholstery. Overall, this chair has one of the best build qualities on the market.

![Great quality chair](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-4.jpg)Great quality chair

* * *

### 4\. Leap Adjustments

One of the reasons the Leap V2 consistently ranks as a great chair for most people is how adjustable it is. The seat height drops to 15.5″ and raises to 20.5″, fitting users roughly 5’2″ to 6’6″ tall. A seat slider adjusts the depth of the seat pan to accommodate different leg lengths. The tilt limiter offers five settings to control how far back you can recline, and tilt tension lets you dial in how much effort it takes to lean back.

![Making adjustments](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-5.jpg)Making adjustments

Steelcase offers three arm options: no arms, height-adjustable only, and 4-way adjustable. We strongly recommend the 4-way arms as they’re probably my favorite armrests overall. Height, width, depth, and pivot are all adjustable, giving almost anyone the ability to find a comfortable position. These arms are a genuine differentiator for the Leap.

* * *

### 5\. Seat Back

One of my favorite components of the Leap V2 is the seat back. It’s one of the best in the business for lumbar support. The side knob lets you adjust lumbar tension significantly, and you can really feel the difference in the lower back. If you want less pronounced support, dial it down; if you like firm support, ratchet it up. The lumbar support is also height-adjustable for precise positioning. As a side note, our VP Ryan didn’t initially like the lumbar feel — he simply removed the support entirely and now loves the chair. That kind of flexibility is rare.

![The seat back is comfortable](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-7.jpg)The seat back is comfortable

* * *

### 6\. Leap Headrest

Personally, I dislike the headrest on the Leap V2 and that’s been true since the first time I sat in the chair. It doesn’t provide the support I’m looking for and actually feels like it pushes my head forward. The only time I marginally appreciate it is in a deeply reclined position. The headrest also has a tendency to slip from where it’s set over time. At $180 as an add-on, I wouldn’t recommend it unless you’ve tried it and know it works for your body.

![The headrest on the chair](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-8.jpg)The headrest on the chair

* * *

### 7\. Leap Comfort

Build quality and adjustments only matter if the chair is actually comfortable and fortunately the Leap V2 delivers. The seat has a concave design that molds around you, and the flexible waterfall front edge prevents you from feeling locked in. Press on the sides or front of the seat and you’ll see that it flexes meaningfully. This allows you to move throughout the day and promotes better blood flow to the legs.

![Thin seat pad](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/steelcase-leap-review-2022-9.jpg)Thin seat pad

# What is the best office chair for someone over 6Ft tall?

![What is the best office chair for someone over 6Ft tall?](https://crandalloffice.com/cdn/shop/articles/BEST-OFFICE-CHAIRS-FOR-TALL-PEOPLE.png?v=1730947486&width=1600)

Ryan Snyder \|
August 13, 2024

**For someone over 6 feet tall, it’s important to find an office chair that offers proper support, especially for the back, neck, and legs. Here are a few high-end office chairs that are well-suited for taller individuals:**

## **1\. Herman Miller Aeron (Size C):**

• **Key Features:** The Herman Miller Aeron is a classic ergonomic chair, and it comes in three sizes (A, B, and C). Size C is designed for taller and larger individuals, offering a deeper seat and higher backrest.

• **Adjustability:** The Aeron provides excellent lumbar support, adjustable armrests, and a seat that accommodates longer legs. Its PostureFit SL back support system is particularly beneficial for taller users.

• **Comfort:** The mesh material keeps you cool, and the chair’s design promotes good posture, even during long hours of sitting.

### **2\. Steelcase Leap v2:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Leap v2 is highly adjustable, with a flexible backrest that conforms to your movements, ensuring constant support.

• **Adjustability:** The Leap v2 offers a seat depth adjustment, which is crucial for taller users to ensure proper leg support. The backrest height and lumbar support are also adjustable to fit your spine’s natural curve.

• **Comfort:** The Leap v2 is known for its all-day comfort and support, making it a great choice for tall users who spend extended periods seated.

### **3\. Humanscale Freedom Headrest Chair:**

• **Key Features:** Designed by Niels Diffrient, the Humanscale Freedom is an ergonomic chair that automatically adjusts to your posture and movements without manual controls.

• **Adjustability:** The headrest is particularly beneficial for taller individuals, as it adjusts to provide neck and head support when reclining. The seat depth and backrest height adjustments accommodate longer legs and torsos.

• **Comfort:** The Freedom chair’s dynamic recline and minimalist design provide continuous support and reduce strain, making it ideal for taller users.

### **4\. Steelcase Gesture:**

• **Key Features:** The Steelcase Gesture is designed to support a wide range of postures and body types, making it a versatile option for tall individuals.

• **Adjustability:** It features an adjustable seat depth and armrests that move in all directions, ensuring that tall users can find a comfortable and supportive position. The backrest provides excellent lumbar support and adjusts to your posture.

• **Comfort:** The Gesture is praised for its overall comfort and ability to accommodate various sitting styles, which is particularly beneficial for taller users who may need extra space.

### **5\. Haworth Zody:**

• **Key Features:** The Haworth Zody is a highly ergonomic chair with a focus on sustainability and comfort.

• **Adjustability:** It offers seat depth adjustment, lumbar support, and backrest height adjustment, all of which are crucial for taller users. The Zody’s pelvic support system also helps maintain good posture.

• **Comfort:** The Zody is designed to provide personalized support, making it a comfortable choice for taller users who need a chair that adapts to their body.

### **6\. Knoll ReGeneration:**

• **Key Features:** The Knoll ReGeneration is a modern ergonomic chair that supports active sitting, making it a great option for those who move frequently throughout the day.

• **Adjustability:** It offers seat depth adjustment, lumbar support, and flexible armrests that adapt to various postures. The chair’s design accommodates taller users by providing ample seat depth and a supportive backrest.

• **Comfort:** The ReGeneration’s flexible design and supportive mesh back make it a comfortable option for taller individuals who need a chair that moves with them.

### **Considerations for Tall Users:**

• **Seat Depth:** Ensure the chair has a deep enough seat to support your thighs without cutting off circulation.

• **Backrest Height:** Look for chairs with adjustable or tall backrests to provide adequate support for your upper back and shoulders.

• **Lumbar Support:** Adjustable lumbar support is crucial for maintaining good posture, especially for taller users who may need the support higher up on the backrest.

Affiliate Disclaimer: We independently review everything we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

We have been [selling big and tall office chairs for over 15 years](https://www.btod.com/Big-And-Tall-Chairs.php). From chairs that start at $200, to high-end options that retail for up to $3,000, we’ve seen almost everything available.

Having sold office seating this long, one thing has become clear, there is no single best option for everyone. Instead, there are a handful of options ranging in price that should suit most user’s needs.

Whether you are big, tall or both, our best chairs for big guys lists list should have something to fit your needs.

* * *

### TL;DR: The 20-Second Verdict

We’ve been selling big and tall office chairs for over fifteen years. The category is more complicated than most people expect and weight capacity alone does not tell you whether the chair will fit.

- **The Good:** The Concept Seating line is the best-built in the category. The 3152HR handles 550 lbs with legitimate ergonomic adjustments, and the 3156HR handles 1,000 lbs for extreme applications.
- **The Bad:** Chairs rated for 400 lbs at standard dimensions won’t fit someone 300+ lbs comfortably. Seat width and seat height are as important as the capacity number.

**Bottom Line:** Start with seat width and seat height for your body, then confirm capacity is at least 10% over your current weight. Warranty and ergonomic adjustments follow from there.

### 1\. Concept Seating 3156HR

**Starting Price:** $3,498.38 + Free Shipping **Where to buy:** [Buy on BTOD](https://www.btod.com/cs-3156hr)

Our number one overall pick is the Concept Seating 3156HR. This big and tall office chair is not for everyone, but it is hands down the strongest chair we offer. Rated for up to 1,000 lbs., it is overbuilt and designed to last a long time. While there are other products on the market that are rated at 1,000 lbs., none are quite like the 3156HR.

A chair this size typically doesn’t come with adjustments, but that’s not the case with the 3156HR. It includes a bariatric tilt mechanism, with three seat angle positions and two separate back positions. There is also a seat depth adjustment which offers four depth options.

Height adjustment on the 3156HR is done by turning a large hand wheel, which adjusts the height of the screw jack. Once the position is found, you can tighten the jam nut with the attached handle. There is 3″ of height adjustment on the bariatric chair. As you can tell from the description, it’s unlike any other chair you’ve read about.

The 3165HR also comes with the same fully articulating headrest on the 3152 HR listed above. This provides plenty of flexibility, no matter how you like to use your headrest.

**Might Not Be a Great Fit For**

At over $3,000, the 3156HR bariatric chair is not in the budget for everyone. If you’ve had issues breaking other chairs in the past, this is a solid investment to avoid those problems.

Because of the capacity of the chair, making adjustments isn’t as intuitive as other products in the list. They are more design to provide customization to fit one user, with the intent of setting it up and not changing again.

The 3156HR is overbuilt throughout the entire chair. Because of this, it’s not the most pleasing to the eye. Of all the chairs in the list, it is the least attractive.

* * *

![#2 Best 24 Hour Use Big and Tall Computer Chair](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/big-tall-chairs-2-best-24hr-use.jpg)

### 2\. Concept Seating 3152HR

**Starting Price:** $2,159.38 + Free Shipping **Where to buy:** [Buy on BTOD](https://www.btod.com/CS-3150HR.php)

Our top pick for 24-hour use, the Concept Seating 3152HR is a workhorse. One of our bestselling 24-hour chairs, the 3152HR is solid and currently manufactured in Wisconsin. The 3152HR comes with a 550 lb. weight capacity and at first glance it’s hard to believe it’s not rated for more.

Featuring a unique seven leg base, the additional legs create easier movement and allow for better stability than most five leg alternatives. The ease of movement is especially important for those that are closer to the capacity of the chair.

While it wasn’t picked as the best for ergonomics, the 3152HR was close to making the cut. Featuring seat height, seat depth, five position tilt lock, an adjustable height backrest, inflatable lumbar and fully articulating headrest, the list goes on. The arms can adjust an additional 2.5″ wider, for a total of 5″ overall width adjustment. The swing away T arms option provide a solution for those who don’t always like to use armrests.

The fully articulating headrest is one of the most unique we’ve tested on any model. It can be adjusted to be used as a neck roll, headrest or rotated out of the way completely.

**Might Not Be a Great Fit For**

Because the seat pan is only 23″ wide, it might not be a great fit for all users. The Dymetrol suspension seat provides good support for long periods but can make the chair feel a bit narrower than 23″ wide.

Built for durability, the aesthetics of the 3152HR are not for everyone. If you’ve had issues breaking chairs in the past, that’s probably not as big of a concern. If you’re looking for something sleek, this is not the chair.

If you’re adding this chair to a shared work environment with users under 5’6″ tall, you should consider adding the partial foot ring option. This will give shorter users the ability to properly support their feet, while keeping a normal chair feel for those that don’t. This feature is available for an added cost of $114.84.

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/mfL2IRHF27rhr4J_-_ZzqxEST7eUWtQBYoYzofpAhKNHsoX_jP9xJEzv3-mVOWj0V1-H8YThBg=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

It’s the most sought-after price point and can also be the most disappointing. Recently, I bought five highly rated chairs on Amazon in hopes of finding a diamond in the rough. Full transparency, I actually bought eight chairs in total. But three of them are from the same brand, Colamy. I first found this brand a couple of years ago while searching Amazon for sleeper picks.

The [Colamy Atlas has been a perennial sub $300 pick](https://www.btod.com/blog/colamy-atlas-top-chair-comfort/) ever since. I’m going to save these three new chairs for the end as a bonus. One thing worth keeping in mind as you read through this list — if you can stretch your budget to the $500–$650 range, our [refurbished Steelcase Leap V2 and Amia chairs](https://www.btod.com/refurbished/) are a completely different class of chair and worth a look before committing to something new off Amazon.

* * *

### TL;DR: The 20-Second Verdict

I identified Amazon office chairs that get high ratings but deliver poor value based on actual testing and long-term user feedback.

- **The Good:** Avoiding bad chairs saves money and frustration. This list highlights chairs with inflated reviews, poor durability, inadequate adjustability, or misleading marketing that creates false expectations.
- **The Bad:** Amazon’s review system makes it difficult to separate genuine quality chairs from those with manipulated ratings. Even chairs with thousands of positive reviews can have fundamental design flaws.

**Bottom Line:** Don’t trust Amazon review scores alone for office chairs. Look for honest long-term reviews from users who have owned the chair for at least six months.

### Big Boy 7000 Series

![Big Boy 7000 Series Amazon office chair overview](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-1-30-screenshot.jpg)

I’m calling this first chair the “ [Big Boy 7,000 Series.](https://amzn.to/48E5vww)” In typical Amazon fashion, this chair, direct from China, has no real name. Just a BIG and TALL 700lbs chair. It is currently $139 with free shipping and has an extra coupon on it for a limited time.

It comes with the most thickly padded seat I have seen on an office chair, ever. And when you sit down in it, it actually has some good spring back to it, not just a thick pad. They say it has a twenty-eight spring system built into the cushion, which is honestly crazy considering the price point. If you’re curious about how seat cushion quality varies by price, our [cheap vs. expensive seat cushion comparison](https://www.btod.com/blog/office-chair-cushions-cheap-expensive/) breaks it all down.

![Big Boy 7000 Series W-shaped seat cushion detail](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-0-53-screenshot.jpg)

The W-shaped seat cushion is interesting, and they say it enhances the curve of your buttocks?! Not sure I’m into that. The overall design makes it feel a bit smaller than 23.22″ wide to be honest. The seat pitches back a bit, which may result in your back legs feeling a lot of pressure.

![Big Boy 7000 Series armrest and lumbar support](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-0-59-screenshot-1.jpg)

It features four-d armrests and an adjustable lumbar support system built into its mesh backrest. I wouldn’t recommend sitting in this if you’re over 350 lbs, because A.) I doubt it’s big enough, and B.) I don’t think it can support that much weight.

* * *

### Tralt Chair

![Tralt ergonomic office chair from Amazon](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-1-51-screenshot.jpg)

The [Tralt chair](https://amzn.to/495gNLQ) has to be one of the most popular chairs on Amazon right now. With over two thousand being sold in the last month alone, it appears a lot of people have this one in their office. It is listed at $169 on Amazon, but has a $30 coupon you can clip to it.

The backrest on this chair is REALLY comfortable. It has depth-adjustable lumbar as well, which works well. The two-way adjustable headrest has nice size to it and allows you to find a good fit for upright tasking and when in recline mode. If you want to see how headrests compare across price points, check out our [office chair headrest tier list](https://www.btod.com/blog/best-office-chair-headrests-tier/).

![Tralt chair seat pad thickness close up](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-3-5-screenshot.jpg)

The seat pad is a bit on the thin side. While it was comfortable for sitting in during the time I tried it, I would be a bit concerned about how long it would hold up. This is pretty common around this price point, though.

![Tralt chair armrest pivot and adjustment detail](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-2-3-screenshot.jpg)

The armrests have some depth adjustment and pivot back and out of the way. If you play guitar or don’t like to use armrests, this might be a solid option. But the pads on them are cheap and flatten out immediately if you plan to use them.

This chair comes in a ton of parts. It was, without question, the hardest of the eight I purchased to assemble.

* * *

### Holludle

![Holludle ergonomic mesh chair from Amazon](https://blog.btod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/I-Bought-5-Top-Rated-Office-Chairs-On-Amazon-Under-300-2-41-screenshot.jpg)

[Holludle’s ergonomic mesh chair](https://amzn.to/3XPu8BI) is our third chair and comes in at $169, but also has a $20 coupon available at the moment. For a cheaper chair, this is probably the best-looking of the bunch. There are a handful of color options available as well.

Everything about this chair feels oversized and extra soft.

# What is 6/2 in its simplest (or lowest) form?

![Flexi Avatar](https://www.ck12.org/flexi/flexi-full-circle.svg)

Flexi Says:

## **Simplifying fractions**, also known as **reducing fractions**, involves reducing the numerator (top number) and the denominator (bottom number) to the smallest possible numbers while maintaining the same value. This process helps make calculations easier and results more understandable.    The fraction 62 can be simplified by finding the highest common factor (HCF) that both the numerator and the denominator can divide by evenly, resulting in a simpler equivalent fraction.    \#\#\# Steps to Reduce Fractions to their Lowest Terms or the Simplest Form    A fraction is in simplest form, or lowest terms, when the numerator and denominator have no common factors other than 1.    To reduce 62 to its simplest form, follow these steps:    **Step 1:** Identify the highest common factor (HCF) of 6 and 2.    **Step 2:** Divide both the numerator and the denominator by their HCF.     6÷2=32÷2=1        **Step 3:** The simplified fraction is 31.    **Step 4:** Convert the simplified improper fraction to a mixed number or whole number. If the numerator is a multiple of the denominator, the result will be a whole number with no remainder.    **Step 5:** Since there is no remainder, the result of the division is a whole number, and the fraction 62 is equivalent to 3.    To learn more about reducing fractions to their lowest terms or the simplest form, [click here](https://flexbooks.ck12.org/cbook/ck-12-cbse-maths-class-6/section/5.2/primary/lesson/types-of-fractions/)!
